title: SceneMI Motion In-betweening for Modeling Human-Scene Interaction
one_line: 场景感知扩散模型处理人体-场景交互，但泛化性有限。
innovations: Dual scene descriptors for global and local context
Diffusion-based motion in-betweening with noisy keyframe handling
Application to real-world HSI reconstruction from monocular videos
method_framework: SceneMI uses a conditional diffusion model with global voxel grid and local BPS features to encode scene context, specialized denoising for noisy keyframes, and U-Net with AdaGN for motion synthesis.
experiment_framework: Evaluated on TRUMANS (clean) and GIMO (noisy real-world) datasets, comparing with MDM, OmniControl, CondMDI, and SceneDiffuser using FID, foot skating, jerk, MJPE, and collision metrics.
takeaways: Dual scene encoding strategy enhances generalization
Diffusion model's denoising capability effectively handles noisy keyframes
Method shows strong performance in real-world applications
weaknesses: Limited evaluation on diverse scene types beyond indoor environments
Training only on TRUMANS dataset may limit generalization to more complex scenarios
relevance_reason: 人体-场景交互建模与可靠性主线无直接交点
